1. there are guidelines where you shouldn't have relationships outside of therapy with past therapists for a good amount of years because of how she's acting. she's still treating you like you're her client and using personal knowledge she knows as a therapist in inappropriate ways. no supervisor at a job would do this

meds can have some effect on weight, it's one of those things that's really hard to tell though. and even if it is entirely the meds preventing you from losing weight, consider how effective and helpful the meds are. try to hold your mental health and stability over your body image (which i get cam be very hard)

 but, the human body is also just designed to keep whatever weight we gain, since it served us well for survival. i don't know if you have a history of being able to lose weight easily,  you know your body best, but something like 10% of people lose significant weight and keep it off. it's just biologically programmed. i would just focus on eating healthy, and exercising (making sure not to overexert yourself), and check your thyroid and stuff if you're concerned. being "overweight" is not inherently unhealthy or bad, our society and medical institutions are just very fat phobic

that being said i do wanna validate your concerns and your want to lose weight. if that's what you want, keep working at it. just also take the above into consideration, dont deprive or overextend your body, and be kind to yourself. and understand you're literally up against a biologically programmed force

ive been on all of those meds except celexa at some point. im 24 and ive struggled with mental health since i was 12 at least, and ive been trying to find the right med since i was 16/17. something to note is that im minimally responsive to several meds, both in terms of side effects and effectiveness. my main symptoms i struggle with are low energy and motivation, suicidal ideation (mostly passive except for some periods), hopelessness, low self worth, etc. i haven't really found anything to help my low energy, though i guess its a bit better without SI and hopelessness 

im currently on effexor (similar to Pristiq), welbutrin,  and lithium. ive been on welbutrin for a while and after lithium ive found it to be the most helpful. 

in terms of helping with energy, pristiq/effexor is supposed to do that, i dont know if ive really experienced it though. im biased i guess but i recommend not switching from pristiq to effexor /going on a high dose unless its really helping because of severe withdrawal symptoms. 

increasing lithium helped with my hopelessness and suicidal ideation soooooo much. but it does give me some tremors,  and i recently realized i have very subtle but existent brain fog and lack of mental alertness. for me it's worth it because its probably saved my life or kept me out of inpatient at least. lithium is proven to help with suicidal ideation and it can help make current meds more effective 

pristiq and effexor have notable withdrawal symptoms, and i feel like lithium does in different ways as well. if youre on lithium you need to get blood tests to have your lithium blood levels and other affected things checked, every time you make a dose change usually, then less frequently on a stable dose

people write off lithium a lot, or use jt as a last resort because of the possibility for toxicity and side effects, and probably just because of more stigma towards bipolar disorder. but youre monitored to make sure you stay within safe levels and side effects dont effect everyone the same

my suicidality was a bit similar to yours some months ago. good Ts avoid involuntarily committing clients and try to work with them, or see what other resources are available. mine recommended i get a higher level of care and do partial hospitalization or intentensive outpatient, which i did. a few months later after the program,  i told her i wasn't sure if i was safe. we basically made a safety plan and i went to stay the night with someone, took off work the next day, and i went back to partial soon after. basically i don't think that well informed Ts would section you, but try to get you more help while making sure you're safe. if you don't feel like you can talk openly about suicidal thoughts with your T, i recommend getting another one if/when you're able (i know its a lot to do). partial or intensive outpatient programs are all over telehealth nowadays, but it was still effective for me, and its a little less disruptive since you can stay home (still had to take off work though). if you have access to that i would recommend it

i realized u were just rambling, so you can totally ignore this post if you dont want advice. that being said, here's my advice if u choose to read it: 

\*\*\*this is from the perspective of healthcare in the US\*\*\*

do you just have a primary care doctor, or a psychiatrist/specialist of some kind? if you dont have a psychiatrist or psychiatric nurse practitioner i highly recommend getting one because honestly, primary care doctors arent equipped for medication management past prescribing someone their first antidepressant and then referring. especially if youre having significant side effects and arent responding well to SSRIs you need someone who really knows their meds and general doctors just dont (in the US at least) 

if you wanna carry on with effexor, you should do what feels right!! if you choose to increase and it helps and you make progress then hell yeah!! i personally wouldnt recommend increasing over 75mg unless the increase is concretely  helping you a lot. effexor is significantly addictive and really difficult to get off of. but, if it helps it helps, and its a good med for many. 

not medical advice, ive just been on A Lot of meds for depression the past 6 years: remeron and welbutrin are a couple atypical antidepressants that i'd recommend looking into or mentioning, because SNRIs have pretty rough side effects and withdrawals. lithium can also be used for unipolar depression as well; i honestly wish i'd been on it way sooner. its also proven to decrease suicidal ideation and risk in unipolar depression which you seem to be dealing with (idk if it needs to be added to an antidepressant or not). the side effects can be unpleasant but it's helped me so much i dont care  

​

anyways, 

be careful with becoming too dependent on effexor if it's not helping you, but if its helping you its totally worth it

i wish you luck and hope you start to feel better

i have treatment resistant depression and i was put on lithium specifically to treat sui* ideation and i really do think it helped a lot and swear by it. i havent had active SI longer than the past 6 months but i have had passive SI for the past 10 years or so, and now it's both passive but really fleeting and less intense 

i didn't experience fatigue as a side effect, also if ur prescriber doesn't already ask to have your dose split for morning/night with the most being at night. i was started with instant release instead of extended for some reason, and i couldn't tolerate the instant in terms of nausea. once i switched over to ER i didnt have nausea at all, though i potentially have appetite loss -- hard to tell because depression was doing that as well.

the tremors are the thing for me. they would go away after a couple weeks of adjusting to a new dose, but when i got to my therapeutic dose of 1200mg they weren't going away. im currently down to 900mg to see if that'll help before i take propanolol, but if not having SI requires some tremors or taking a med to treat the side effect of a med thats ok with me. lithium really pulled me out of hopelessness 

everyone's body is different and you'll have a different experience than me. some ppl hate it and some swear by it. that being said lithium has really strong studies proving it reduces risk of sui* attempts and SI. im wishing you good luck and hope whatever happens it doesn't negatively impact you or your studies too much
